question.text: The first Persian invasion of Greece was led by this Persian ruler in order to punish them for their participation in the Ionian Revolt. This man divided his empire into satraps.
question.clue: After his predecessor died of gangrene, this king and six other nobles assassinated a magician pretending to be Bardiya named Gaumata, an event described in his cliff-face Behistun Inscription.

swap.leadin: A military operation in this country called Operation Eagle Claw was authorized only when Secretary of State Cyrus Vance took a brief vacation and was not present to oppose the plan.
swap.text: Name this country that took 52 Americans hostage in 1979 and released them moments after Ronald Reagan was sworn in as President in 1981.
swap.clue: This country was invaded by neighboring Iraq to limit the power of its Shia majority.

question.text: Leonidas' 300 Spartans were defeated by this empire's much larger force: over 2 million troops if you believe Herodotus, which scholars don't. Xerxes [zerk-zees] led this empire against the Greeks, but was defeated at the naval Battle of Salamis.
question.clue: One ruler of this empire famously ordered the ocean to be whipped.

swap.text: The losing forces and Issus and Gaugamela were led by a ruler of this name, though he supposedly fled out of fear at both battles. Another ruler of this name fathered Xerxes the Great, and was Cyrus the Great's nephew.
swap.answerHtml: Darius [accept Darius III or Darius the Great or Darius I]
swap.clue: A successor of Cambyses II ("kam-BYE-zees the second") with this regnal name founded a capital at Persepolis.

question.leadin: After the Iberian War in 532, this empire signed the Perpetual Peace with a neighbor to its west.
question.text: Name this empire whose leader Khosrow I signed that treaty. Procopius, a neighboring empire's most famous historian, recorded that the treaty was broken within a decade in the Lazic War.
question.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the general Belisarius.
swap.text: At the Battle of Dara, Belisarius defeated forces under this empire, who were known for their heavy armored horsemen called cataphracts. Later, the Byzantine Empire established the Eternal Peace with its leader Khosrau I (KHOO-shuh-roo "the first").
swap.clue: One king of this dynasty was crowned in utero, while another may have either flayed the skin of a noted captive or poured molten gold down his throat after forcing him and his army to work on an aqueduct, the Band-e-Kaisar.

question.leadin: This man named 16 cities after his father, Antiochus.
question.text: Name this general who served under a famous Macedonian king during his Asian campaigns. He was also the first ruler of a namesake empire, the easternmost of the Macedonian successor states.
question.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

swap.leadin: Troops of this empire poured molten gold down the throat of a captured commander.
swap.text: Name this empire that won the Battle of Carrhae while commanded by Surena and Silaces.
swap.clue: It fought several wars against Tigranes the Great, who ruled (+) Armenia to the west, using its heavily armored cataphracts.

question.text: Important to both the Medes and Persians were this priestly class which accomplished feats of prophecy, dream-interpretation, and sorcery later named for them.
question.clue: Darius' rise to power is described in the Bisitun inscription, which claims that Gaumata, one of these people, pretended to be Smerdis, the brother of Cambyses II. These people, who in Sasanian times were led by a chief figure called the mowbed, are described by Herodotus as one of six Median tribes.

swap.text: By dethroning his grandfather Astyages, Cyrus ended this empire, which was led from Ecbatana. Under Cyaxares, this empire took part in the conquest of Neo-Assyria.
swap.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

question.text: The Sassanids proselytized this state religion of theirs, though it did not spread as far as Manichaeism or Christianity. This religion venerates Ahura Mazda.
question.answerHtml: Zoroastrianism [accept Mazdayasna or Mazdaism; do not accept or prompt on "Mazdakism"]
question.clue: This religion whose followers began converting to Islam after the fall of the Sassanids and Arab conquest of Persia.

swap.leadin: The third and fourth kings of this name were separated from their rule by Pharnaces I.
swap.text: Give this name for six kings of Pontus, the last of whom massacred 80,000 Romans in Anatolia and prompted Sulla, Murena, and Lucullus to fight three namesake wars against him.
swap.answerHtml: Mithridates [or Mithridates the Great; or Eupator Dionysius from any confused folks]
swap.clue: After conquering the territory of Nicomedes IV of Bithynia, a king of this name massacred all of its Roman citizens in the "Asiatic Vespers".

question.text: The Behistun inscription is written in Old Persian, Babylonian, and the language of these peoples, whose capital was Susa. This civilization's Old dynasties included the Awan, Simashki, and Epartid.
question.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

swap.text: Many Neo-Hittite states to the south spoke this Semitic language that replaced Akkadian to become the lingua franca of the Near East
swap.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

question.text: The Parthian ruling dynasty was named after this founding ruler, who ruled from the city of Nisa after he conquered a satrapy from the anti-Seleucid rebel Andragoras.

swap.text: This Parthian Spahbed was victorious at Carrhae. He was later killed by Orodes II because his success constituted a threat to his authority
swap.clue: According to Plutarch's Parallel Lives, a commander fighting against this leader had to rescind an attempted charge when he saw that his soldier's "hands were riveted to their shields and their feet nailed through and through to the ground" by arrows.

question.leadin: George Rawlinson re-read Strabo's claim that these people required that men must have at least five wives as a misinterpretation of a limit on the size of their harems.
question.text: Heleen Sancisi-Weerdenburg quipped that what people's short-lived empire "exists for us because Herodotus said it did," referencing the historian's questionable accounts of kings like Deioces and Astyages?
question.clue: Early kings of these people included Deioces and Phraortes.

swap.text: An "archaeological complex" named for Bactria and this region was home to Gonur Depe ("go-NOOR deh-PEH"), where Harappan seals have been found. A much later mention of this region's name appears in the Behistun Inscription, which records the rebellion of Frada there.
swap.answerHtml: Margiana [or Marguš or Margush or Margiane or Marv; accept Bactria-Margiana Archaeological Complex; accept Frāda of Margiana]

question.leadin: Answer the following about a kingdom in Asia FTPE.
question.text: Ecbatana was the capital of this kingdom, which was absorbed into Cyrus the Great's budding Persian Empire around 550 B.C.
question.clue: The city of Nineveh was captured by his successor Cyaxares, who extended this kingdom's borders to the Halys river in Asia Minor.

swap.text: Parthian rule ended after this local ruler of Istakhr overthrew Artabanus V and established the Sassanid Empire. This father of Shapur I built a namesake palace as well as the Maiden Castle in the city of Fars, and skirmished with Alexander Severus's forces to the West.
swap.clue: This man, whose early life is the subject of a "book of deeds" or Kar-Namag written in Middle Persian, was the son of a lord of Fars named Papak.
